images.title: Sorting by angles
images.purpose: Show acute-angled, right-angled and obtuse-angled triangles by their largest angle.
images.composition: Three triangles in a row with equal spacing, the largest angle of each highlighted, names below and white space around.
exact_structure: Left: an acute-angled triangle with angles 50°, 60° and 70°, all three angles marked with small green (#009E73) arcs, the 70° arc in reddish purple (#CC79A7) labelled 70°.
Middle: a right-angled triangle with angles 90°, 50° and 40°, the 90° corner marked with a reddish purple square labelled 90°, the other two with small green arcs.
Right: an obtuse-angled triangle with angles 120°, 30° and 30°, the 120° angle marked with a reddish purple arc labelled 120°, the other two with small green arcs.
All three share one baseline; thin dark outlines, light fills, no other numbers.
rejection: an angle value other than 70°, 90° or 120° for the highlighted angle
the right-angled triangle having no square corner
images.takeaway: A triangle is named by its largest angle; acute-angled means all three angles are acute.
images.description: Three triangles with their largest angles 70°, 90° and 120° highlighted.
images.context: Shown beside the concept text and video for this concept.
images.teaching_notes: Find the purple angle first; it decides the name.

image_decisions.why: The biggest angle decides the kind of triangle.
